The difference is that we are abstraction machines. A photon hits our retina at one time and means one thing. A photon hits the same place at another time and is interpreted as another. This abstraction of physical processes is what allows the machine characterized by the atoms, molecules and cells that make up our brain to free itself from classical determinism. This means that 'we' are more than just the physical processes in the brain, we are a symbol system and turing machine built from the physical processes in the brain. There may be no soul, but there is software as well as hardware.

From there it gets murky, and this is my opinion, well informed and thought out as it may be. The recursion isn't simple recombination of existing inputs and outputs. We theorize. We try completely different things. We may completely invert our thinking, just to see what happens. We may rearrange things randomly, or combine unlike things to attempt to understand them in a different way (a very good example would be thinking about light and electricity as like items, or poetically representing people as telephone poles or trees). That isn't to say these processes are magical, they seem to be algorithms. The really interesting thing is that we seem to be able to generate these algorithms ourselves. And they don't seem to be either completely dependent on input, nor completely random in nature.

I think there will eventually be a system defined for this process, but we haven't come far enough to develop it yet. A type of mathematics for thinking about things and generating new ways of thinking about things. And like mathematics there seems to be an infinite number of ways you can combine symbols with rules for operating on those symbols to generate different ways of thinking, and they seem to be all tied together though they may not all be able to exist in the same 'universe' at once. And we can skip around within those different systems. We can use those systems to decide on which system to use, and then use those systems to generate further systems. And because we aren't bound by consistency, we can use one to get to another, almost like the type of math you see come from paranoid schizophrenics. Because there isn't one system to rule them all. One person may choose one branch, while another will choose another, based only on their internal experiences manipulating systems in the past. When you add subjective valuations, this results in something very much like free will, or at the very least a stochastic process which may produce different results based on the exact same initial inputs.

That being said, all of this free will isn't necessarily good for us. It would probably do us good to be a little more logical, a little more consistent, and little more complete in our thinking, and this would make us much more effective in dealing with the outside universe. But there will always be areas with room for inspiration and inconsistency, such as music, or poetry, or the visual arts.

This may not be 'hard' free will, but it is certainly not determinism either. I would call it 'soft' free will, and it seems to explain the most human psychic phenomena, while still staying grounded in reality and not invoking magic, or souls, or any other clear nonsense.
